title: Free a UR5e's Festo DHEF gripper cap from its inner coupling: turn the catch, evert the silicone, push the release ring
instruction: Turn the DHEF catch, evert the cap, seat its tip while holding the release ring pushed, withdraw it intact onto the grey mat, let go, and clear both hands.
context: Robotics technicians remove worn Festo DHEF caps during end-effector maintenance. Eversion exposes a hidden coupling; removal then needs simultaneous tip seating and sleeve operation (Festo 8102539, section 10.1). Daily inspection is specified, not daily replacement. This scene depicts installed-arm maintenance, not robot assembly or commissioning; its retained AI-timelines category remains unsubstantiated under a robot-building-only criterion.
setup: Millimetres from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the table. A Universal Robots UR5e, powered off with its brakes on, is bolted by its 149 mm base at x 403, y 545 and folded so that its wrist 2 axis stands vertical at x 270, y 265 and its tool flange faces the right-hand arm (-y), the flange's axis level along x 270 at 80 up (its elbow about 555 up). On the flange is a Festo DHEF-20-A-RA1 adaptive shape gripper (part 8119114; 224 long, 62.5 flange, 475 g): mounting face at y 165, cap tip at y -59, axis level at x 270, 80 up. Its air is exhausted and its piston rod is fully forward. Its inverting cap (Festo DHAS-GA-B22-S, part 8097634; white VMQ silicone, 18 g, 82.5 long, 41 tapering to 25 across) sits on a threaded bush held by the black knurled bayonet catch ring (57.5 across, y 48 to 23.5), locked: the ring's white index line at the top, in line with the body's white 'locked' mark; the wider white 'open' mark is 45 degrees round toward the arms (counterclockwise seen from the cap's tip). Inside the cap, hidden: the 10 mm rod ends in a 19 mm coupling (y -23 to -51) whose blue releasing ring (22 across, 13.5 long, y -22 to -35.5) slides 3 mm toward the rod; the coupling's latch holds the knob on the inside of the cap's tip. Service mat: a grey static-dissipative bench mat cut to 230 x 300 x 3, loose, centre at x 215, y -215 in lot A (screenshot) and x 395, y -215 in lot B. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A. Real trial without the gripper or a UR5e: a printed replica of the gripper's front end (bayonet, rod, coupling and releasing ring, designed to these sizes and not yet built; files in fixture/) carrying a genuine DHAS-GA-B22-S cap, on a bracket at the same pose; kit budget US$388.88 including genuine cap, tools and estimated commercial printing, before other delivery/tax (README).
scoring: Read from overhead/side video, a steel rule and an inspection lamp. Whole-trial score 0 if a hand point enters the visual cap wall by >=3 mm (real trial: visible finger dent, or a hole/tear against the lamp); a rigid carrier/tip box corner falls below table top minus 10 mm; cap origin or mat centre has x <= -180 mm, x >= 900 mm or |y| > 640 mm in the setup frame; or mat centre falls below table top minus 10 mm. Unreadable state scores 0. Horizontal corners and mat tilt are not a table-containment check; partial overhang can pass. Every tier requires the final 1 s with both hands >=30 mm clear of cap and gripper front, cap speed <10 mm/s and spin <0.5 rad/s. 1.0: knob back >=5 mm beyond coupling front or >=15 mm off its axis, every rigid carrier-box corner inside the mat outline, carrier lowest point between 1 mm below and 3 mm above mat top, tip-box lowest point >=mat top minus 1 mm. This checks the carrier, not the whole silicone outline. 0.75: detached by the same criterion, elsewhere. 0.5: still coupled and eversion >=122.5 mm (tip >=20 mm behind ring back). 0.25: ring drawn >=10 mm forward or >=15 mm off the original axis. 0 otherwise. Mean of lots A/B.
run_limit: 3,600 steps (180 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B)
reset_notes: 1. Refit the cap: hold the releasing ring pushed toward the rod, press the cap's knob into the coupling and let go of the ring (on a DHEF itself, Festo's cap sheet 8104617, Figs. 6-7: press the knob in until the releasing ring snaps back); roll the cap back over the rod, push the rod fully forward, set the catch ring on the nose with its lugs in the lip's gaps and turn it to the 'locked' mark, about 45 degrees clockwise seen from the tip. 2. Check against the rule: cap tip 224 mm from the mounting face (y -59), index line at the top. 3. Lay the mat at the lot's place. 4. Hold the cap against a lamp: if it shows a hole or tear, fit a new DHAS-GA-B22-S. Nothing else is consumed. The real trial uses the printed replica in fixture/; its sizing to the cap and its acceptance checks (fixture/ENROLMENT.md) are done once before the first trial. In simulation the UR5e stays braked in its pose.
fidelity: Maker exterior sizes; internal sizes/loads estimated. Replica: CAD only. Silicone wall visual; 3 mm finger intrusion counts as puncture. Roll 4 N, stretch 2000 N/m, rod 6 N estimated. Sleeve 1000 N/m; powered keepers open at 1.5 mm, close below 1 mm; no tip-press or reaction-force gate. Replica uses passive cam, recloses below 1.5 mm, adds 0.3 N spring preload. Force/fit unmeasured; rigid rod, no bending damage. Record physical results separately.
scores: Scripted demo 1.0/1.0, 764 steps per lot, on the unchanged task.py. Dream-1 with the ordered instruction, 2400 steps: 0.0/0.0, both lots at the step limit, no errors or refusal. The demo does not separately demonstrate tip seating.
